items.name: Book One · Excel for Absolute Beginners
items.note: From your first cell to a summary you can show someone. Parts 1 to 12, lessons 1 to 78.

items.name: Book Two · Excel PivotTables and Dashboards for Absolute Beginners
items.note: From a long list of rows to a one-page dashboard. Parts 13 to 20, lessons 79 to 155.

items.name: Book Three · Excel Power Query for Absolute Beginners
items.note: Clean your data once, then refresh it every time. Parts 21 to 28, lessons 156 to 232.

Practice: Copying a Formula Down the Sales Sheet

XLOOKUP: Finding a Value in a List

parts.name: Dates and text

publishing.description:
Three books, one volume, 232 short lessons. Everything a complete beginner needs to go from never having typed in a cell to a clean, refreshing report someone else can use.

This collection holds the full text of all three Excel guides in the Absolute Beginners series:

Book One, Excel for Absolute Beginners: from your first cell to a summary you can show someone. Workbooks and sheets, typing and formatting, formulas and functions like SUM and XLOOKUP, sorting, filtering, tables and your first chart.

Book Two, Excel PivotTables and Dashboards for Absolute Beginners: from a long list of rows to a one-page dashboard. The Field List, grouping dates, showing values as shares and running totals, PivotCharts, slicers and a timeline.

Book Three, Excel Power Query for Absolute Beginners: clean your data once, then refresh it every time. Junk rows, stray spaces and dates stored as text, whole folders of files, unpivot, append and merge, and fixing a query when the source changes.

These titles have been previously published as standalone books.

Every lesson is one idea on one page, with a clear diagram of what is actually happening and one small thing to try before moving on. The practice pages all use the same small example, a corner shop's year of sales. No unexplained jargon, no assumed expertise.
publishing.audience: Complete beginners who have never used Excel, or use it only to type lists.
